title: Leading-Digit Hailstone Dynamics
headline: A Collatz-adjacent leading-digit dynamical system with an open universal convergence conjecture and a formally verified conditional restriction on hypothetical accelerated cycles.
description: This project studies the map $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=3n+2L(n)+1$ for odd $n$, where $L(n)$ is the leading decimal digit. Exhaustive computation through 5,000,000 and targeted adversarial tests found no competing positive cycle, but universal convergence to the distinguished 7-cycle remains a conjecture. The Lean 4 development formally specifies the map and proves that any positive accelerated periodic orbit whose odd states are all at least 5,000,001 has at least 971 distinct odd states.
verification: The Stage-2 formal specification is audited, and the conditional 971-state accelerated-cycle restriction is proved in Lean from the map-specific cycle equations and explicit minimum-state hypothesis. The central universal convergence conjecture remains unproved; Palomar editorial remediation is ongoing.
attribution: This repository records John Fairfax-Ball's research programme on the leading-decimal-digit-controlled hailstone map, including computational investigation and Lean formalisation. Historical novelty of the full map remains unresolved.
original_source: The distinguished 7-cycle is classical 5x+1 behaviour on single-digit odd inputs. The cycle analysis uses established Collatz-cycle product-window and continued-fraction/Farey methodology, especially Eliahou (1993) and Simons–de Weger (2005); no exact prior source for the full leading-digit map has been identified in the current audit.
